headlines.label: Overtakes
headlines.detail: On track after lap 1 · most: VER (11)

summary: Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix from pole position, 14.6s ahead of Max Verstappen, with Isack Hadjar completing the podium.
Max Verstappen made the biggest climb, from P21 to P2.
Oliver Bearman had a day to forget, dropping from P6 to P17.
The stewards penalised ALB (5 second time penalty) and HUL (10 second time penalty).
There were 58 pit stops in total; the winner stopped 3 times.
Rain fell at some point during the race.
Kimi Antonelli leads the championship by 111 points over Max Verstappen.
aiSummary: Lando Norris converted pole into a commanding São Paulo Grand Prix victory, crossing the line 14.6 seconds clear in cool conditions, with rain falling at some point and both intermediates and softs in play. The headline act behind him, though, was Max Verstappen, who scythed from 21st on the grid to second, making 11 of the race's 85 overtakes. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull, while Kimi Antonelli slipped from second to fifth but set the fastest lap, a 1:12.689 on softs on lap 55. Oliver Bearman endured a miserable slide from sixth to 17th, and Antonelli's championship lead over Verstappen stands at 111 points.
